Kozelets Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Kozelets already had several Jewish households by 1666, growing to a community of 2,702 by 1910, supported by a Talmud Torah and synagogues. Kozelets was the birthplace of two notable figures: Yehuda Leib Tsirelson (born 1859), Chief Rabbi of Bessarabia, member of the Romanian parliament, and prominent Halakha scholar; and Yuri Davidovich Levitansky (born 1922), a poet and translator known for lyric and burlesque work. The cemetery, appearing on Russian maps from the 1880s and fenced by the ESJF in 2015, remained in use until as recently as 2008, its last burial; Holocaust victims from the area are buried in a mass grave at its entrance.
